title: New Collective Quantified Goal on climate finance

definition.text: The new climate finance target, negotiated at COP29 in 2024, for supporting developing countries after 2025, building on the earlier $100 billion a year goal.

facts.text: The earlier goal, set in 2009 and agreed at Cancún in 2010, was for developed countries to mobilise US$100 billion a year by 2020 for developing countries.
That target was missed in 2020 and reached only in 2022; an OECD report gave $132.8 billion in 2023 and $136.7 billion in 2024.
At COP29 in Baku, delegations agreed that developed nations would pledge $300 billion a year by 2035, from public and private sources.
Poorer nations called this insufficient and many pushed for at least $500 billion; some critics, including UN officials, called it a betrayal.
A key tension was the donor base: the US and EU wanted countries such as China and the Gulf states to contribute, but the text only encouraged voluntary contributions.
Talks at COP30 were expected to address scaling finance from the $300 billion agreed in Baku to $1.3 trillion.

contested_note: Developing countries and critics called the $300 billion figure too small, while developed countries pressed for a wider donor base.
